Meenakshi Modi and Neha Ghemawat Modi said the Supreme Court had barred any arrest or coercive action and promised to appear. 114: Order of 26 September 2023 for accused Indu Tak, No. 164. She had been allowed on 29 August 2023 to travel abroad, but could not go without her passport. 115: Two orders of 30 September 2023 for accused Indu Tak (No. 164) and Megha Chauhan (No. 163), both represented by advocate Bhim Singh Motsara. 116: Order dated 16 November 2023: no one present. Routine adjournment only; nothing else decided.
117: Hearing of 9 February 2024 before Judge Roopam. Accused Shinder Pal Singh (137) never appeared despite the High Court's direction, and repeated notices came back unserved, so the court ordered him declared wanted through a public proclamation (Section 82), to be put up by 20 March 2024, with the constable to report on 1 April 2024. 118: Short order of 1 April 2024 before Judge Roopam. The police constable (ASI Sunil Kumar) who was told to publicly put up the proclamation declaring accused Shinder Pal Singh (A-137) wanted/absconding came to court and his statement about publishing it was recorded. Case adjourned to 3 May 2024, the date already fixed, for the appearance of Shinder Pal Singh.
119: Hearing of 3 May 2024 before Judge Roopam. Shinder Pal Singh (137) still did not show up after the 30-day public proclamation period, so he was formally declared a proclaimed offender (absconding/wanted) and police informed. SFIO did not object to Shivraj Sharma's request for a pardon to become a prosecution witness, so it was allowed and he must come to give his statement. Thirteen accused were permanently excused from attending court; Raj Kumar Bohra's exemption requires him to report monthly at the Indian Embassy in Dubai and seek permission before visiting other countries. Bailable warrants for Priyanka Modi and Padmawati Art Creation came back unserved.
120: Order of 3 May 2024 allowing accused Raj Kumar Bohra to travel abroad. He said he is an NRI whose wife Nita Bohra, who suffers from severe depression, and three children live in Dubai, UAE; he is managing partner of RKC International General Trading LLC and travels to UAE and Bangladesh for export business. SFIO opposed orally. Since he had travelled and returned on time on earlier permissions, the court allowed travel after 3 May 2024 on condition of security of property or bank guarantee worth Rs 1 crore, forfeitable if misused. Surety Ajay Kumar Arora agreed to continue.
121: Order of 4 June 2024 before Judge Jagdeep Singh. Accused Jainam Rathod came in person and handed his passport back to the court after it had been released to him. The court took the passport on record and ordered release of his Rs 2 lakh fixed deposit (FDR) that he had given as security when getting the passport, after a photocopy is kept on file. File to be put up on 29 July 2024.
122: Hearing of 29 July 2024 before Judge Jagdeep Singh, mainly attendance and adjournment to 3 September 2024. SFIO was told to file the death report of accused Virender Modi by then. Jailed accused, and those on bail here but held in other cases, to be produced by video link. Thirteen accused excused for that day only but warned to attend next time. Neha Ghemawat and Meenakshi Modi, who had promised to appear, instead filed a bond application; they must produce any higher court stay order or appear in person. Siddharth Chauhan told to file the High Court order protecting him. Priyanka Modi and Prakash Chander Purohit sought permanent exemption.
123: Hearing of 3 September 2024 before Judge Jagdeep Singh. Shiv Raj Sharma's statement may be recorded before a Duty Magistrate. Neha Ghemawat, Meenakshi Modi and Siddharth Chauhan got a last chance to show protective orders or face action for avoiding court.
124: Hearing of 13 November 2024 before Judge Jagdeep Singh. SFIO filed the death certificate of accused Virender Modi showing he died on 18 May 2022, so the case against him was closed (abated). SFIO was told to file an amended case title listing pardoned accused as prosecution witnesses. Shiv Raj Sharma had failed to go before the Duty Magistrate for his approver statement but was said to be ready. Neha Ghemawat and Meenakshi Modi, who still had not appeared or shown any protective order, and Siddharth Chauhan got one last chance. Many accused excused for that day; jailed accused produced by video link. Next date 18 January 2025.
125: Order of 3 December 2024. Accused Megha Chauhan (Tak), No. 163, filed an application asking for her passport back and for permission to travel to South Korea. 126: Order of 13 January 2025. SFIO asked the court to declare accused Siddharth Chauhan a proclaimed person (absconding/wanted), because the High Court had dismissed his petition on 9 January 2025. The court only had the application registered and listed it with the main case on 24 January 2025; no decision yet.
127: Hearing of 18 January 2025 before Judge Jagdeep Singh. Jodhpur jail did not produce Mukesh Modi, saying he was on interim bail till 1 March 2025, though neither this court nor the High Court had granted it; the court sought a detailed report from the Jodhpur jail superintendent. Siddharth Chauhan's High Court petition was withdrawn on 9 January 2025; he cited treatment at Fortis Hospital, Gurugram, and was given 30 days, until 27 February 2025, to appear or face being declared absconding. Neha Ghemawat and Meenakshi Modi relied on Supreme Court protection from arrest, but were told to show a court-attendance stay or appear, failing which coercive steps.
128: Hearing of 27 February 2025 before Judge Jagdeep Singh. Siddharth Chauhan sought to be excused, but his anticipatory bail petition had been withdrawn in the High Court on 25 February 2025; the court rejected his request and ordered him to appear by 7 April 2025 under the earlier public proclamation, or face consequences. Neha Ghemawat and Meenakshi Modi again neither appeared nor produced any Rajasthan High Court order; the judge agreed their bond application was not maintainable while they defy the court, issued fresh summons and warned of coercive steps, as the case is stalled by three absent accused. Jodhpur jail still had not explained Mukesh Modi's supposed interim bail.
129: Order dated 3 April 2025: no one present. The judge, Jagdeep Singh, was going to be on casual leave from 4 to 7 April 2025 (6 April being a Sunday), so the case was simply adjourned to 3 May 2025 for the same purpose, with all concerned to be informed. Routine adjournment only.
130: Order dated 2 May 2025: no one present. Routine adjournment only; nothing else decided.
131: Order dated 29 May 2025: no one present. The judge, Jagdeep Singh, would be on casual leave on 31 May 2025, so the case was simply adjourned to 22 July 2025 for the purpose already fixed, and everyone concerned was to be informed. Routine adjournment only; nothing else was decided that day.
132: Hearing of 19 September 2025 before Judge Jagdeep Singh. Jodhpur jail had released Mukesh Modi claiming interim bail, though he has no bail in this case; the court said the jail superintendent appeared to be helping him unlawfully and sought a report from Rajasthan's Home Secretary by 6 November 2025, warning of a contempt reference. Non-bailable arrest warrants against 14 accused, including Nitin Rathore, Abhay K. Shah, Aditya Sarda, Nazima and Shabbir Khan, came back unexecuted and were reissued; the Khans' plea to pause was refused for lack of a stay. Siddharth Chauhan cited a Supreme Court stay but did not appear. Jainam Rathod is jailed in Sabarmati, Ahmedabad.

Excuses for absence (fever, back pain, eye injury, Mumbai seminar; Meenakshi Modi caring for husband Mukesh Modi after knee surgery; Neha Ghemawat's spine surgery advice) allowed for that day only, proof required. Pleas by Aditya Sarda, Nazima and Shabbir Khan to pause the case rejected without a stay; arrest warrants reissued as homes were locked.
134: Hearing of 7 January 2026 before Judge Gagan Geet Kaur. Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi, freed from Jodhpur jail on Rajasthan High Court interim bail although the Punjab and Haryana High Court dismissed their bail here on 22 December 2025, sought medical excuse; refused, bail bonds forfeited, arrest warrants issued, medical papers to be verified, AIIMS Delhi check-up ordered. Meenakshi Modi (caring for husband) and Rohit Modi (caring for wife after surgery) also refused, bonds forfeited, arrest warrants issued. SFIO asked that Shiv Raj Sharma be accepted as approver. Warrants against 14 others postponed over a Supreme Court no-coercive-action order. Siddharth Chauhan's surrender-and-bail plea rejected as he was absent.
135: Order of 20 February 2026 before Judge Puneet Sehgal, after the case was transferred to him. Accused Megha Chauhan (No. 163) had applied to get her passport back from the court so she could apply for a US visa. Arguments on her request were not heard that day and it was adjourned to 25 February 2026 for consideration. No decision yet.
136: Order of 20 February 2026 before Judge Puneet Sehgal, after transfer of the case. Accused Indu Tak (No. 164) had applied for release of her passport held by the court so she could apply for a US visa. Arguments were not heard that day; the request was adjourned to 25 February 2026 for consideration. No decision yet.
137: Order of 25 February 2026 before Judge Puneet Sehgal. The Supreme Court had on 17 February 2026 given accused Siddharth (Chauhan) a final extension to surrender by 20 February 2026, failing which police could act. The court clerk reported he had not surrendered despite this, so the court issued a non-bailable arrest warrant to bring him before court on 18 March.
138: Short record of 25 February 2026. The lawyer for accused Indu Tak (No. 164), Neeraj Dev Gaur, stated that he was withdrawing her application for return of her passport (sought for a US visa) because it had become pointless (infructuous), keeping the right to file a fresh one later. The arrest warrant against Siddharth Chauhan came back unserved, so a fresh non-bailable warrant was issued for 17 April 2026. The judge dismissed the request because she did not state any purpose for the Vietnam trip, which he found to be deliberately concealed.

Following the High Court's 22 December 2025 order, SFIO must list who has and has not appeared, so the trial of absent accused can be separated. Eleven absent accused summoned by bailable warrants of Rs 10,000.
142: Order dated 30 May 2026 before Judge Yashwinder Paul Singh: no one present. Because the judge was going on summer vacation from 1 to 15 June 2026, the case was simply adjourned to 10 July 2026 for the purpose already fixed, and all concerned were to be informed. Routine adjournment only.

144: Hearing of 29 July 2026 before Judge Yashwinder Paul Singh, mainly an attendance table of all 187 accused. Adjourned to 19 August 2026.
145: Hearing of 19 August 2026 before Judge Yashwinder Paul Singh. SFIO filed an amended list of parties. Mukesh Modi and Rahul Virendra Modi, wrongly released from Jodhpur jail without bail in this case, were found to be evading court, so the court ordered them declared wanted by public proclamation: read out and pasted at their homes and the court, and published in a newspaper at SFIO's cost, requiring them to appear on 8 October 2026. The case was listed on 7 September 2026 to record their statements about carrying out the proclamation.
148: Short order of 7 September 2026. The SFIO clerk did not turn up, so the prosecutor got a date of 8 September 2026 to record statements on how the public proclamation against Mukesh Modi and Rahul Virendra Modi was carried out. The judge found the court clerk (Ahlmad) had failed to issue the non-bailable arrest warrants ordered against Bharat Modi and Bharat Vaishnav, and warned him to be careful. The prosecutor sought time to check their status.

SFIO Assistant Director Yashika Sharma handed the papers to law consultant Sandeep Kumar Yadav, who read them aloud and pasted them at Gurugram's new court building on 3 September 2026, then flew to Udaipur and went by taxi to their last known address, A-10 Adarsh Nagar, Sirohi, Rajasthan, pasting them on the boundary wall and announcing them in the main market. Their appearance stays fixed for 8 October 2026. Bharat Modi, possibly in Jodhpur jail, to be produced; fresh arrest warrant for Bharat Vaishnav via DCP (HQ).
